title: Lord of My Life! O May Thy Praise
description: Lord of My Life! O May Thy Praise in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 940 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord of my life! O may thy praise Em-ploy my no-blest powers, Whose good-ness length-ens out my days. And fills the cir-cling hours!

lines: Lord of my life! O may thy praise
Whose goodness lengthens out my days.
I passed the shades of night,
Serene and safe from every harm,
While many spend the night in sighs
In gentle sleep I close my eyes
When sleep death's semblance o'er me spread,
Thy watchful care was round my bed,
O let the same almighty care

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
